# Herald

> Herald turns one server (a VPS, a Raspberry Pi, any Linux box with Docker) into a git-driven Docker Compose host. A push to an app repo deploys its stack. A push to the server repo reloads config and redeploys what changed. One `config.yml` in git describes everything that runs on the server.

Herald is a single Go binary that runs as a systemd service. It has no database and no web UI for configuration. It reacts to GitHub webhooks, or to `git push` into a bare repo on the server. It wires Caddy for TLS and routing, resolves age-encrypted secrets, and runs `docker compose up`. Docker owns the runtime; Herald owns the path from push to running containers.

## Model

- Everything Herald manages is a **stack**: a Docker Compose project with a domain, secrets, and one source.
- The source is either `repo:` (a GitHub repo, `owner/name`) or `path:` (a directory in the server repo that contains a `compose.yml`). Never both.
- Repo stacks track `branch:` (default `main`) or a fixed `tag:`, never both. `tag_pattern:` auto-deploys matching tag pushes and needs `branch:`.
- Path stacks redeploy on a server repo push only with `auto_deploy: true`, and only when their directory changed. `update:` runs a script after `compose up`.
- `preview:` works on repo stacks only and needs a wildcard domain. Previews get no secrets. Pull requests from forks never start a preview.
- The same repo can be deployed several times under different stack names, branches, tags, or domains.
- Containers are named `herald-<stack>`. Use plain `docker compose` / `docker logs` for logs and exec; Herald does not wrap them.

## Minimal config

```yaml
server:
  name: srv1
  deploy_domain: deploy.example.com   # only needed with GitHub webhooks
  services_dir: /opt/deploy
  acme_email: ops@example.com

stacks:
  myapp:
    repo: myorg/myapp
    branch: main
    domain: myapp.example.com
    secrets:
      - key: myapp/db_password
        target: DB_PASSWORD
        type: env
        generate: alphanumeric        # created on the server at first deploy
    preview:
      enabled: true
      domain: "*.preview.myapp.example.com"

  nextcloud:
    path: stacks/nextcloud
    domain: cloud.example.com
    auto_deploy: true
```

## Secrets

- Secrets live age-encrypted on the server, never in the repo. Config only names them by `key`.
- `generate:` lets the server create a value on first deploy, so nobody has to see or type it.
- Otherwise an operator sets it on the server: `herald secret set <key>`.
- `type: env` puts the value in the stack's `.env`. `type: docker-secret` writes a Docker secret file.

## Commands

```
herald                      Where setup stands and the command to run next
herald init [owner/repo]    Bootstrap from a server repo (no argument: bare repo on the box)
herald deploy <stack>|--all Deploy stacks
herald down <stack>         Stop and remove a stack's containers
herald sync                 Pull server repo, reconcile config and webhooks
herald status               Stacks, domains, health
herald doctor               Diagnose problems, print fix commands
herald secret set|list      Manage secrets
herald preview list|remove|cleanup
```
